title: Analytics stores accept a query logger and a results logger whose indices match, so an asynchronous query can be paired with its own result
content:
Every `IAnalyticsStore` implementation — `KnexAnalyticsStore`, `PostgresAnalyticsStore`, `MemoryAnalyticsStore`, `BrowserAnalyticsStore` — takes two optional logging hooks in its constructor options:

```ts
const queryLogger   = (index, query)   => console.log(`[Q:${index}] ${query}`);
const resultsLogger = (index, results) => console.log(`[R:${index}] ${JSON.stringify(results)}`);
const store = new MemoryAnalyticsStore({ queryLogger, resultsLogger });
```

The detail that makes them useful rather than noisy: **"since queries are asynchronous operations, indices match between query and results functions."** So a log line can be paired with its own result even when several queries are in flight — which is exactly the case where an unindexed log is useless.

`defaultQueryLogger(tag)` and `defaultResultsLogger(tag)` are the included implementations, appending a tag to each line so two stores in one process stay distinguishable.

For measurement rather than debugging there is `IAnalyticsProfiler`, consumed by each store, with a default `AnalyticsProfiler` in `@powerhousedao/analytics-engine-core` and a `PassthroughAnalyticsProfiler` for when profiling should be inert.

Why this matters beyond convenience: these stores generate SQL from typed TypeScript objects, so the logger is the only way to see what a dimensional query actually became — which is where an unexpectedly slow rollup usually explains itself.
